commits.summary: Bind input lengths before accepting a proof and retain its assumptions
commits.body:
Require a length-sensitive beside-route proof to use a bound declared by its frozen claim or task, or the versioned planner default committed in the job's source-claim link. A result cannot supply its own missing bound. Check witness values without counting the number of arguments as an array length. Report the provenance and carry evidence limits and checker assumptions independently into the JSON and text milestone views.

All 51 acceptance tests and all 22 milestone tests passed, including bound drift, replay membership, ordinary defaults and a compatibility check on an existing beside-route task. The human report for 287 now shows the termination assumption on its preservation evidence.

commits.body:
Example 308 pins the release class, source blob, independent subsequence oracle and mutation patch. On JDK 21 the release JAR and source rebuild agreed on all 225 inputs, while the shared-row control disagreed on 44. Its score on ab and aa changed from 1 to 2. javap confirmed the two-dimensional allocation at offset 18 on each build.

Both ordinary JVM replay tasks passed and published receipts, including 44 mismatches for the altered artifact. The native transfer probe reached the multidimensional allocation and refused it at unwind 18 and array bound 4. Its outcome and measured cost are recorded independently of the frozen claim. The example validator and all four router and contract checks passed.

commits.summary: Isolate submission identity in the pipeline test
commits.body: The test inherited the real Codex thread ID when exercising its synthetic Claude session, so it failed on this worker. Clear both identities in the fixture and cover the actual precedence when a Codex worker inherits a parent session. The formerly failing case and the affected pipeline test file passed.

commits.body:

Class initialization observations refuse the known indirect property reads, dynamic member lookup and unbound CPU, filesystem or charset settings in the initialized classes. The four exception and six initializer countermodels now have named refusals on the checker and independent JVM controls. The changed Rust suite, focused JVM tests and inventory lint passed.

The replay returns its own observation descriptors, actual values and root identities. The evidence routes compare complete descriptors, alias policy, input bounds and bound environment against the independent plan.

The independent JVM counted 0, 3 and 21 differences across all 71 heaps. Native established the return-only claim and both poststate witnesses reproduced on the JVM. Forced per-argument cloning, an omitted comparison and a swapped observer each failed the independent mapping check. All 47 changed-suite groups passed before the final evidence-telemetry adjustment, whose affected ingestion and qualification cases were rerun. The example validator and tier lint passed.

commits.summary: VF-045: a Codex worker can pick up the run-brief skill by itself, since nothing marks it as one only a person starts
commits.body: In the first minute of the single-agent Codex run foundation-domain-streams, the agent said it would use the run-brief skill. It read the skill and ran brief_run.py status, which is read-only, then chose to work on the brief directly, starting nothing. Only publish and review-findings are marked as started by a person alone, for both clients. run-brief, single-agent-run, prove-java-change and run-verification are not. Recorded as minor, at the user's word, to address later by a skill change or by rewording how a run is invoked.

commits.summary: A review of the Python architecture around jvmcontract, as a brief for a fast-follow run
commits.body: Copied unchanged from the user's planning folder (in-the-loop-python-proof-architecture-review.md, reviewing 2fd3369f). It recommends keeping Python for planning, preparation, controls and evidence, and refactoring where a declared claim becomes a jvmcontract invocation. It names a concrete gap: the ordinary equivalence command drops a claim's input assumption, shown on 307, where three distinct claim keys produced one identical command. Its implementation order: fix the gap with two benign fixtures and a field audit; a typed invocation model, with 307 migrated in shadow runs; the adapter boundary on 289; and result decoding extracted, with comparable attempts. It is meant to follow the foundation work now under way. Its links are pinned to commit 2fd3369f on GitHub.
